description: Lets the build harness merge itself: `github-actions` and `gradle-wrapper`, majors included. Extend it AFTER the base preset — `"extends": ["github>youndie/sborka", "github>youndie/sborka:automerge-harness"]` — because package rules are concatenated in that order and the last match wins, and this one has to win over the base preset's rule that sends every major to a human.

The argument: a major of actions/checkout is not the same kind of event as a major of a library this repository publishes. The harness ships to nobody, and the check that would catch a bad bump is the build itself, which already ran on the pull request.

WHICH IS THE PRECONDITION, AND IT IS NOT RHETORICAL. This is only safe in a repository where a pull request actually runs that build. Before extending this, look at what runs on `pull_request` in the repository doing the extending — in the workflow, not in a sentence about it. mongkn was the counter-example here for months: its build workflow was `workflow_dispatch` only, so a green-looking pull request meant nobody had run anything. Its triggers went back on, this text did not notice, and the repository kept citing a reason that had expired — which is the second lesson and the reason the first sentence says to go and look.

EXCEPT THE RUNNER LABEL. The `github-actions` manager also reads every `runs-on:` label (datasource `github-runners`), and a label is not harness in the sense above: it decides the OS, the libc and the system packages a workflow builds against, and the workflows most sensitive to it — publish, release, image — are exactly the ones a pull request does not run. mongkn#17 merged itself on 2026-10-01 and moved its `workflow_dispatch`-only publish.yml from ubuntu-24.04 to 26.04, where libmongoc is 2.x under other library names; the next klib would have linked against a floor no consumer had, and every check on that pull request was green because none of them ran publish.yml. So a runner label falls back to the base preset's human gate, in a group of its own so that it does not hold the actions majors with it (youndie/sborka#126).

GitHub's own auto-merge is deliberately not used (`platformAutomerge: false` in the base preset): it refuses to arm on a branch with no required checks, and adding branch protection to `main` would change how these repositories are worked in. Renovate merges the pull request itself instead.

packageRules.description: The build harness merges itself, majors included: CI on pull_request is the review.

description: A runner label waits for a person, majors and all: no pull request runs the workflow it matters to most, so the build that would catch it is not the one that ran.

AFTER the rule above, because the last match wins. Its own group because Renovate merges a grouped pull request only when every update in it may merge: left in `ci actions`, one held label would hold every action major beside it, which is not what this is for. `verifyHarnessPreset` in sborka's `check` fails if a later rule hands the label back to automerge, or if this group goes away.
